main_text.p: gregationis seu Capituli nostri genera[?] decreto mittitur ad sedem Apostc[?] cam, ut ei exponat quasdam constit[?] tiones nostras jam à sacra Congregati[?] ne regularium examinatas & approb[?] tas, atque ut earundem constitutione[?] confirmationem apud sedem Apostoli[?] prosequatur negotium, cujus causa R[?] mam legatur, personamq; ipsam quan[?] possum animi effectu E V. commend[?] negotium illi curæ fore dubitare non[?] nit ea E.V. benevolentia, quam in omn[?] bus rebus suis experta est Congregat[?] nostra. Personam autem ipsam cum pr[?] bitatis & scientiæ omnis generis lau[?] præstet, gratiosam illi futuram confid[?] Ejusmodi homines apud E. V. lon[?] commendatione opus non habent; e[?] enim eorum asylum & columen;quapr[?] pter cæteris, quæ in eo laudari possu[?] omissis, Deum Opt. Max, precor, ut [?] minentiam Vestram quam diutissimè E[?] ecclesiæ suæ conservet.

page.notes: The right edge of the scan cuts off the last letters or words of most lines (for example "genera", "Apostc", "constitutione", "commend", "lon", "possu"). These ends are marked [?] or cut at the scan edge and could not be read; the printed words likely continue beyond the crop. "approb" and "quan" are partly visible and uncertain. Lines 1 and "ecclesiæ" at the start of the last line are partly cut at the left edge as well. The catchword "EPIST" is cut off at the right edge and is probably the beginning of "EPISTOLA" on the next page. Long s is transcribed as plain s; the ligature & is printed as & in the text.
